Beyond Boundaries From Demarcations to Dignified Coexistence

The Responsive Panel

Beyond Boundaries

From Demarcations to Dignified Coexistence

Every cigarette put out in the bin leaves a trail on the frosted-glass panel. The trails drift, gather and slowly fade, so the space quietly shows how much smoking has passed through it.

The context

Smoking is a personal choice, but in Singapore regulations shape where it is permitted. Yet many designated smoking areas offer little beyond a yellow box and a sign: they mark where smoking happens, but give nothing back. The panel is one part of Beyond Boundaries, an adaptable spatial system that reimagines the smoking area through greenery and subtle consciousness.

Inspired by contrails

The visual comes from the trail of smoke a jet leaves across the sky. Right behind the plane it is crisp and bright; further back it breaks apart, softens and drifts, and it is still there long after the plane has gone. Each dispersion on the panel behaves the same way: one cigarette, one trail, released from the centre of the glass and gradually fading, a trace of something that has already passed.

Beyond graphic warnings

The idea grew out of the graphic images on cigarette packaging and the guilt-tripping tone of anti-smoking ads. Knowing the consequences does not always lead to change, and shock is easy to tune out. Moving beyond graphic health warnings, the panel takes a metaphorical approach instead: abstract art that does not single anyone out, but lets smokers see their shared, accumulating impact and become a little more conscious of smoking's harmful effects.

Encouraging reflection, not enforcing change.

How it works

  1. Detect A smoke sensor integrated in the bin registers each cigarette as it is discarded.
  2. Translate The reading becomes one new trail, stronger when there is more smoke.
  3. Visualise The panel builds up over time, with older trails fading as new ones arrive.

Alongside the sensor-integrated bin, modular seats and spatial planters, the panel forms one system of four elements that can be arranged as the Enclave, the Nook or the Trail: from demarcations to dignified coexistence.
